newsitem.title: FRANCE: France predicts NATO-Russia accord by May 27.
newsitem.headline: France predicts NATO-Russia accord by May 27.

text.p: French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette predicted on Tuesday that NATO and Russia would conclude an agreement on a new partnership redefining Europe's security order in time to be signed in Paris on May 27.

"Some real difficulties remain to be resolved, but I believe we will succeed," de Charette told reporters in Strasbourg, eastern France, after meeting Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov there on Tuesday morning.
Primakov went on to Luxembourg on Tuesday afternoon for key talks with NATO Secretary General Javier Solana aimed at resolving the final obstacles to a new NATO-Russian charter.
"I am hoping for a successful meeting," the Russian minister told reporters on arriving at Luxembourg airport.

The Western allies want the charter, which gives Moscow a permanent consultative role with its old cold-war enemy, to form the centrepiece of a new security order in Europe and alleviate Russian concerns over the alliance's planned enlargement into eastern Europe.
Moscow strongly opposes likely NATO membership for Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic and seeks commitments from NATO setting clear limits on military activities within the new members' borders.
